hints: Combine the logarithms using the power and quotient laws before removing them.
Write \(-1=\log_{10}(10^{-1})\) to obtain \((2x+1)/(x+1)^2=10^{-1}\), then rearrange to a quadratic.
Solve the quadratic, check \(2x+1>0\) and \(x+1>0\) for each candidate, and round both admissible roots to 3 decimal places.
walkthrough:
State the given logarithmic equation with base $10$:
$$\log_{10}(2x + 1) = 2\log_{10}(x + 1) - 1$$

Express the constant term $1$ as a logarithm with base $10$:
$$1 = \log_{10}(10)$$

Apply the power law of logarithms to the term $2\log_{10}(x + 1)$:
$$2\log_{10}(x + 1) = \log_{10}\left((x + 1)^2\right)$$

Substitute these into the equation and group logarithmic terms on one side:
$$\log_{10}(2x + 1) = \log_{10}\left((x + 1)^2\right) - \log_{10}(10)$$
$$\log_{10}(2x + 1) = \log_{10}\left(\dfrac{(x + 1)^2}{10}\right)$$

Equate the arguments since the logarithmic function is one-to-one:
$$2x + 1 = \dfrac{(x + 1)^2}{10}$$

Multiply both sides by $10$ and expand the squared binomial:
$$10(2x + 1) = (x + 1)^2$$
$$20x + 10 = x^2 + 2x + 1$$

Rearrange all terms to form a standard quadratic equation $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$:
$$x^2 + 2x - 20x + 1 - 10 = 0$$
$$x^2 - 18x - 9 = 0$$

Solve the quadratic equation using the quadratic formula $x = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$ with $a = 1, b = -18, c = -9$:
$$x = \dfrac{-(-18) \pm \sqrt{(-18)^2 - 4(1)(-9)}}{2(1)} = \dfrac{18 \pm \sqrt{324 + 36}}{2} = \dfrac{18 \pm \sqrt{360}}{2}$$

Check domain validity for both roots ($2x + 1 > 0$ and $x + 1 > 0$):
For $x_1 \approx 18.487$: both $2x + 1 > 0$ and $x + 1 > 0$ are satisfied.
For $x_2 \approx -0.487$: $2(-0.487) + 1 = 0.026 > 0$ and $-0.487 + 1 = 0.513 > 0$, so $x_2$ also lies in the domain of both logarithms.

Round both solutions to $3$ decimal places:
$$x = 18.487 \quad \text{or} \quad x = -0.487$$

ai_rubric.Solving Exponential and Logarithmic Equa: Identifies $\log_{10}10=1$. Reduces to $x^2-18x-9=0$, or equivalent. The final result is $x=18.487$ or $x=-0.487$.
